description: Implement creator post management: backend PUT /posts/:postId (edit) and DELETE /posts/:postId (delete) routes with ownership validation, plus mobile UI for editing and deleting posts from PostDetailScreen.
steps: BACKEND - Add updatePost and deletePost to post.service.js:

- updatePost(postId, userId, userRole, updateData): Find post by ID. Verify ownership (post.authorId.toString() === userId || userRole === 'Admin'), throw 403 if not. Allow updating only: caption, tags, isHumanMade, isNsfw. Process tags same as createPost (parse string/array, lowercase, trim). Save and return updated post. Invalidate feed cache.

- deletePost(postId, userId, userRole): Find post by ID. Verify ownership same as above. Delete: the Post document, all Like docs where postId matches, all Save docs where postId matches, all Notification docs where postId matches, FeaturedPost entry where postId matches. Invalidate feed cache. Return true.
BACKEND - Add updatePost and deletePost controllers in post.controller.js:
- updatePost: validate postId format, call postService.updatePost(req.params.postId, req.user.id, req.user.role, req.body), return 200 with updated post
- deletePost: validate postId format, call postService.deletePost(req.params.postId, req.user.id, req.user.role), return 200 with success message
- Handle 403 and 404 errors same as other controllers
BACKEND - Add routes in post.routes.js (after authGuard):
- router.put('/:postId', controller.updatePost)
- router.delete('/:postId', controller.deletePost)
- Place these AFTER the router.use(authGuard) line and BEFORE or AFTER the interactions routes
BACKEND - Update authGuard.js to include 'role' in req.user object (it already does: req.user = { id: user._id.toString(), role: user.role }), so no change needed there
MOBILE - Add updatePost and deletePost methods to mobile/src/services/post.service.ts:
- updatePost(postId: string, data: { caption?: string; tags?: string[]; isHumanMade?: boolean; isNsfw?: boolean }): Promise<Post> - PUT /posts/:postId
- deletePost(postId: string): Promise<void> - DELETE /posts/:postId
MOBILE - Update PostDetailScreen.tsx:
- Import useAppSelector selectUser from authSlice
- Add state: const [showOptionsMenu, setShowOptionsMenu] = useState(false)
- Determine isOwnPost: post.authorId._id === currentUser?.id
- Change the header '...' button behavior: if isOwnPost, show a menu with 'Edit Artwork' and 'Delete Artwork' options; if not own post, show report modal as before
- For the options menu, use a simple Modal or inline View that appears below the '...' button with two TouchableOpacity items

- Delete handler: Show Alert.alert('Delete Artwork?', 'This action cannot be undone.', [{ text: 'Cancel', style: 'cancel' }, { text: 'Delete', style: 'destructive', onPress: async () => { await postService.deletePost(post._id); navigation.goBack(); } }])
- Edit handler: Navigate to 'EditPost' screen with params { postId: post._id, post }
MOBILE - Create new screen mobile/src/screens/post/EditPostScreen.tsx:
- Form fields: caption (TextInput multiline), tags (TextInput comma-separated), isHumanMade (checkbox/toggle), isNsfw (checkbox/toggle)
- Pre-populate from route params post data
- On save: call postService.updatePost(postId, { caption, tags: tagsArray, isHumanMade, isNsfw })
- On success: Alert 'Post updated', navigate back
- Style consistent with existing screens (darkColors theme, SafeAreaView pattern)
MOBILE - Register EditPost screen in AppStack.tsx:
- Add to AppStackParamList: EditPost: { postId: string; post: Post }
- Import EditPostScreen and add Stack.Screen
- Import Post type from post.service.ts
acceptance_criteria: Ownership check: only post author or Admin can edit/delete
Delete cascades to Like, Save, Notification, FeaturedPost documents
Mobile PostDetailScreen shows Edit/Delete options only for own posts
Mobile EditPostScreen allows editing caption, tags, isHumanMade, isNsfw
Mobile delete shows confirmation alert before proceeding
All backend files pass node --check syntax validation
findings: All backend JS files pass node --check syntax validation. Mobile TypeScript files cannot be type-checked without node_modules but follow existing patterns correctly.
